title: Ellington adopted them; the separation dance and the baptizing walk
summary: Ellington kind of adopted the pair; Green describes their separation dance to Scatting at the Kit Kat and introduces his baptizing walk.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: So, let's go on now. We've covered the Duke Ellington band era for you. Your admiration for the man -- I guess you knew him personally.
Yes. He kind of adopted us.
Was there any step that you had particularly for him -- something special that you'd do for him?
Well, yes, it was a walking, you know, and he called it rhythm, you see. 'He's got rhythm.'
In other words, when he would introduce you, you would do this stuff for him?

No, no, no. It was just doing my dancing. I was tap dancing in my act, you see, 'Scatting at the Kit Kat.' See, now, he was already the composer of this melody, see. But Chuck and Chuckles had -- we had a separtion tap dance we did. Some would call it competitive, you know, or playing or inter-playing, you see.

Yeah, see, they would try to call it this but we didn't -- we called it a separation dance, because each member dancing separately, one first and the other one secondly, like that and back to one, see. Then ending together in some kind of
way, but exiting, you see. Now, I had a walk.
So, you had the walk. I'd love to see that walk, Chuck.
Yes, I could show it to you. It's the baptizing walk, you see. You baptize the taps -- it's walking, you see. I'll get up and try it. It's got room enough to do that walking.
